gui.homelink_farm.help.title: User guide
gui.homelink_farm.help.controller:
# What does the controller do?
It combines information from linked monitors and pumps: crops, maturity, irrigation and problems. It never plants or harvests crops.

# Link your devices
Right-click this controller with the Farm Connector to select it, then right-click each monitor or pump to link it. Devices must be in the same dimension and within range: 64 blocks by default, with up to 32 components.

# Read the results
Figures come from the monitors' latest scans. Rescan requests a new scan from them. If a chunk is unloaded, its last known figures may be marked stale; the controller never forces chunks to load.

# HomeLink and permissions
Use HomeLink: network to select an authorized network. HomeCore can then expose statistics and request remote scans. You need permission to configure this device and manage the networks involved.

# Missing data?
Check device links, monitor zones and loaded chunks. Allow scans to finish. Distance and component limits can be configured on the server.
gui.homelink_farm.help.monitor:
# What does the monitor do?
It counts crops in a zone and reports maturity, irrigation and detected problems. It works on its own or linked to a controller, without planting or harvesting.

# Set the zone
A newly placed monitor watches its whole chunk: 16 × 16 blocks, from the bottom of the world to the build limit. Zone 16×16 restores that area; Clear stops monitoring it. A full pass takes a few seconds.

For a custom zone, hold the Farm Connector and sneak + right-click two blocks to select corners A and B. Then sneak + right-click this monitor. The server limits zone size and distance.

# Read the figures
Ready counts mature crops. Maturity is an average. A partial scan means part of the zone is unloaded. Rescan requests a fresh scan; completing it can take several ticks.

# Diagnose and locate
Diagnostic lists problems such as dry farmland, low light or unavailable irrigation. Click a row to locate that crop in the world. Show zone outlines the monitored area; Show irrigation displays sprinkler coverage.

# Comparator
The Comparator button changes the redstone measurement: maturity, ready crops, irrigation coverage or problem count. Place a comparator against the monitor to read its signal.
gui.homelink_farm.help.pump:
# Set up irrigation
Place the pump next to a real water source, or directly inside one. Connect it to sprinklers using copper pipes. The pump never creates water. Oxidized and waxed pipes work the same way.

# Place sprinklers
Place a sprinkler on a pipe, or click the pipe's underside to hang it below. By default, it covers 5 × 5 blocks: 12 blocks below to one above when standing, or 12 blocks below up to its own level when hanging.

# Capacity and growth
By default, one supplying pump supports 5 sprinklers. Supplying pumps on the same network add their capacities together. Exceeding the limit stops the entire network.

Active sprinklers hydrate farmland and, by default, give compatible crops 20% more growth opportunities. Overlapping sprinklers do not stack this bonus. Range, capacity and bonus are configurable.

# Power and redstone
The power button enables or disables this pump. Redstone mode can ignore the signal, run only when powered, or stop when powered. A comparator reads the sprinkler count while running, or 15 during a fault.

# Troubleshooting
Check the water source, pipe connections, capacity and redstone mode. Another active pump may still supply the network. Show irrigation displays active and offline coverage.

# HomeLink
Link the pump to a controller with the Farm Connector to combine its data. HomeLink: network also enables remote monitoring and control through HomeCore, subject to your permissions.

Zone limits and scan budget of Crop Monitors.
homelink_farm.configuration.maxLinkDista: Maximum distance, in blocks, between a Farm Controller and a linked device.
homelink_farm.configuration.maxComponent: Maximum number of Crop Monitors and Pumps linked to one Farm Controller.
homelink_farm.configuration.maxCropMonit: Maximum number of blocks (X × Y × Z) in a zone drawn with the Farm Connector. The whole-chunk zone is not limited.
homelink_farm.configuration.maxZoneDista: Maximum distance between a Crop Monitor and any block of its zone.
homelink_farm.configuration.cropScanInte: Ticks between two scans of a zone (20 ticks = 1 second).
homelink_farm.configuration.cropScanBudg: Zone positions one Crop Monitor examines per tick.
homelink_farm.configuration.globalScanBu: Zone positions examined per tick by all Crop Monitors together.
homelink_farm.configuration.locateDurati: How long (ticks) a LOCATE marker stays visible.
homelink_farm.configuration.maxSprinkler: Sprinklers one pump can feed (official rule: 5). Above that the whole network is over capacity.
homelink_farm.configuration.maxNetworkNo: Maximum pipes, pumps and sprinklers in one network.
homelink_farm.configuration.sprinklerRan: Horizontal reach: a sprinkler covers a (2 × range + 1) square. 2 = 5 × 5.
homelink_farm.configuration.irrigationGr: Growth speed bonus of irrigated crops (0.20 = +20%). Never stacks.

gui.homelink_farm.help.farmbot_station:
# What does the station do?
It docks, charges and controls one FarmBot, and collects its harvest in a 9-slot output. The robot parks on the block in front of the station.

# Install a robot
Right-click the station with a FarmBot. The spot in front of the station must be free. One station holds one robot; a robot belongs to one station only.

# Choose the crops
Link the station to a Farm Controller with the Farm Connector. The robot then works from the nearest Crop Monitor of that farm; Monitor cycles through the others. The robot never scans the farm itself: it drives to the mature crops the monitor reports.

# Harvest cycle
The robot drives to a mature crop, harvests it, replants it with part of the harvest and looks for the next one. It comes back when its battery reaches 20%, when its 9 slots are full or when nothing is left to harvest, then unloads and charges.

# Commands
Start and Pause allow or stop new tasks. Return home sends the robot back at once. Output shows the harvest; if it is full, the robot keeps its cargo and waits (OUTPUT BLOCKED).

# Recovering a robot
Out of power, a robot stops where it is. Sneak + right-click it to pick it up with its cargo, or push it back onto its dock. Hitting it drops it as an item.
